title: Replicating hallucination concept-probe monitoring on a different domain (code vs. factual QA)

original_idea.body:
# Replicating hallucination concept-probe monitoring on a different domain (code vs. factual QA)

**Problem:** Beaglehole et al. validate hallucination probes on standard benchmarks. Whether a hallucination concept probe trained on factual-QA contrasts transfers to a different hallucination domain (e.g., hallucinated code APIs) is an untested, accessible generalization test.

**Direction:** Fit a hallucination concept probe on factual-QA contrast activations from an open model, then evaluate it on a code-hallucination set (non-existent library/function calls), comparing to an LLM-judge. Twist: cross-domain transfer of the hallucination probe, a domain the original didn't cover.

**Why it matters:** Hallucinated code APIs are a concrete, high-stakes failure (supply-chain/security). A cheap internal probe that flags them without a judge is useful monitoring infrastructure, and cross-domain transfer is the kind of robustness check labs skip.

**Relevant context:** Beaglehole et al. hallucination-probe results; linear-probe hallucination detection; package-hallucination security literature; neural_controllers repo.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain but hallucinated-code/supply-chain security is somewhat tangential to catastrophic AI risk; a skipped step.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probe + cross-domain eval with public datasets, novice+mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused cross-domain transfer test, but building a code-hallucination eval set adds a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: open models/data, robustness check labs skip.

novelty.reasoning: Hallucination probes exist; code-domain transfer angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Hallucination probes exist; cross-domain code transfer partly open.
